TDMV 1.desc: A contemporary approach to beginning-level ballet technique, principles, and terminology. Develops the body for strength, flexibility, and artistic interpretation. Emphasis on developing a foundation in movement for the continuation of ballet training. Historical origin of ballet will be discussed. May be taken for credit six times.
sec: Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building
Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building

TDMV 11.desc: The study of theatrical tap dance. Various styles of tap— such as classical, rhythm, and musical theatre—will be introduced. Emphasis on rhythm, coordination, timing, and theatrical style. Includes basic through intermediate tap movement. May be taken for credit three times.
sec: Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building
Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building
Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building
Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building

TDMV 110.desc: Continued studio work in ballet technique at the intermediate level and terminology. Emphasis on increasing strength, flexibility, and balance, and the interpretation of classical musical phrasing. Includes proper alignment training and artistic philosophy of classical ballet. May be taken for credit six times.
sec: Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building

TDMV 111.desc: A contemporary approach to ballet technique, terminology, and performance at the advanced level. Introduces more complex choreographic variations and skills. Individual and group composition will be examined and aesthetic criticism applied. May be taken for credit six times.

TDMV 112.desc: Designed for students with advanced training in contemporary modern dance and intermediate to advanced training in ballet. Emphasis is on increasing composition and performance skills in ballet through contemporary modern dance aesthetics. May be taken for credit six times.

TDMV 120.desc: The development of contemporary dance as an expressive medium, with emphasis on technical skills at the intermediate level. Includes the principles, elements, and historical context of contemporary modern postmodern dance. May be taken for credit six times.
sec: Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building

TDMV 122.desc: The development of contemporary somatic approaches to dance as an expressive medium, emphasizing advanced technical skills, efficient athleticism, kinesthetic refinement, individual creative voice, and performance elements. Choreography and aesthetic concepts will be explored. Incorporates various principles of human movement research. May be taken for credit six times.

TDMV 123.desc: Students will study the practice of improvisational dancing with a partner. Students will develop skills in giving and supporting body weight, lifting, balancing, falling, rolling, and recovering fluidly together. May be taken for credit three times.
TDMV 123.pre: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.
TDMV 123.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Senior
sec: Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building

TDMV 130.desc: Designed to provide training in the technique of jazz dance, while placing the art form in its historical context as an American vernacular form. Builds an intermediate technical jazz level with a focus on style, musicality, dynamics, and performance. May be taken for credit six times.

TDMV 133.desc: Further development in the technique of jazz dance, while placing the art form in its historical context as an American vernacular form. Builds an advanced technical jazz level with a focus on style, musicality, dynamics, and performance. May be taken for credit six times.

TDMV 140.desc: This course explores African diasporic dance practices, histories, stories, rhythms, and aesthetics depending on the focus of the instructor. Students will engage with principles from techniques and histories that have traversed history and geography. May be taken for credit six times.
TDMV 140.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Senior
sec: Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building
Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building
Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building
Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building

TDMV 141.desc: Courses designed for the advanced continuing study of the dances and historical context of a particular culture or ethnic form: Afro-Cuban, Spanish, Balinese, Japanese, Latin, etc. Specific topic will vary from quarter to quarter. May be taken for credit two times.
TDMV 141.pre: TDMV 142 or TDMV 143 or TDMV 144, or consent of instructor.

TDMV 142.desc: This course explores Latine dance practices, histories, stories, rhythms, and aesthetics. Specific forms of study depend on the focus of the instructor. Students will engage with basic principles of Latine techniques, histories, and social contexts as they have developed and changed over time. May be taken for credit six times.
TDMV 142.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Senior
sec: Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building
Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building

TDMV 144.desc: This course explores the specific dance traditions of East Asia, South Asia, South East Asia, or the Pacific Islands. The course will explore dance practices, histories, and aesthetics depending on the focus of the instructor. Students will engage with basic principles from techniques and histories that have traversed history and geography. May be taken for credit six times.
TDMV 144.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Senior
sec: Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building
Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building

TDMV 146.t: Intermediate Latin Dances of the World
TDMV 146.desc: To develop an appreciation and understanding of the various Latin dances. Emphasis on learning intermediate social dance movement vocabulary, history of Latin cultures, and use of each dance as a means of social and economic expression. May be taken for credit two times.
sec: Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building

TDMV 148.desc: This course is designed to build on the skills developed in TDMV 138, Hip-Hop, also deepening students’ understanding of the social, political, and economic forces at work within hip-hop culture. More complex rhythms and sequencing will be introduced, and musicality will be honed through an added emphasis on freestyle expression. May be taken for credit four times.

TDMV 149.desc: Develops hip-hop skills at the advanced level with further studies of the social, political, and economic forces at work within hip-hop culture. Emphasis is on complex rhythms and sequencing, freestyle expression, choreography, and performance. May be taken for credit six times.

TDMV 190.desc: An in-depth investigation of the role and aesthetics of performer/dancer in a fully staged independent project resulting in a dance performance choreographed by faculty or students. May be taken for credit two times.
TDMV 190.pre: upper-division standing and consent of instructor.

TDMV 2.desc: Introduction to contemporary somatic approaches to dance, building fundamental technical skills, kinetic and perceptual awareness, efficiency, and artistic expression. Choreographic sequences are analyzed through time space coordination and dynamics. Movement exploration includes improvisation and composition. May be taken for credit six times.
sec: Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building
Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building

TDMV 20.desc: This creative laboratory course facilitates group and individual experimentation through the study of somatic movement processes and methodologies. Students explore approaches to movement vocabulary that offer them insights into investigating their own movement generation and dance making material. May be taken for credit six times.
sec: Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building
Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building

TDMV 3.desc: Introduction to the technique of jazz dance, while placing the art form in its historical context as an American vernacular form. Builds a beginning technical jazz vocabulary with a focus on rhythmic exercises, isolations, turns, and locomotor combinations. May be taken for credit six times.
sec: Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building
Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building

TDMV 38.desc: An introduction to the basic technique of hip-hop, studied to enhance an understanding of the historical cultural content of the American form hip-hop and street dances in current choreography. May be taken for credit four times.
sec: Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building
Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building

TDMV 43.desc: An introductory course that explores the history of West African cultures and diasporas through student research, oral presentation, dance movement, and performance. Contemporary African dances influenced by drum masters and performing artists from around the world are also covered. Course materials and services fees may apply. May be taken for credit three times.
sec: Molli and Arthur Wagner Dance Building

TDMV 5.desc: An introduction to the physical practice of yoga. A detailed investigation into the ancient somatic practice of energetically connecting the mind and body through kinesthetic and sensory awareness and how this supports and informs dance practices. May be taken for credit six times.
